1. 기록연대, 배경\n 1) 가장 마지막에 기록된 문서\n - 신약 2:
1. Date of writing, background
 1) The last document written
 - One of the last documents written among the 27 books of the New Testament.
요한 문서는 A.D 90년경 사도들이 다 순교하고 요한 사도만 남아 있었:
John's writings come from c. A.D. 90, when the apostles had all been martyred and only the apostle John was left. After Emperor Nero's persecution had passed, and Jerusalem had been destroyed in the meantime.
 2) When heresies were running wild
헬라어 -영지, 지식으로 번역 됨\n - 영지주의라고 하는 그노시스파가:
Greek - translated as ‘spiritual knowledge,’ knowledge
 - It was written at a time when the Gnostics, the group called Gnosticism, were disrupting the church.
Dualists - separate matter and spirit, treat matter as sinful, and deny creation.
예수님의 인성을 부인-가현설 : 가상의 육체를 입고 오셨다. 성경을 공부: Denying Jesus' humanity - Docetism: he came wearing an imaginary body. If you do philosophy instead of studying the Bible, you become a heretic.
3. 요한복음의 신학\n 1) 로고스의 신학:
3. The theology of John
 1) The theology of the Logos
<요1:1> 태초에 말씀이 계시니라 이 말씀이 하나님과 함께 계셨으니 이: <John 1:1> In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
<요1:14> 말씀이 육신이 되어 우리 가운데 거하시매 우리가 그 영광을:
<John 1:14> And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.
 - Jesus Christ is the Logos
 2) The theology of love
 - The apostle Paul's theology is a theology of faith, a theology of justification by faith.
Peter's theology is a theology of hope.
John's theology is a theology of love.
믿음도 중요하고 소망도 중요하지만 그 중에 제일은 사랑이다.\n3) 예수:
Faith is important and hope is important, but the greatest of these is love.
3) Emphasizes Jesus' divinity
 - It's saying that Jesus wasn't just a powerful prophet; going beyond that, the whole divinity of God was in Jesus. So the direction of John's theology is an interest in the identity of Jesus, who transcends everything.
 - So the words Jesus spoke, and the amazing events, works, and miracles he did, are important, but more important than that, it pays attention to who this person is who exercises such power.
 - In the end, it leads all the way to Thomas confessing, “My Lord and my God.”
 - Finally, it focuses on this: the God who transcends everything and was the Logos from the beginning became flesh, the Son of God who came from above to this earth.
그래서 예수님은 일반 사람으로서는 할 수 없는 말씀들을 많이 하시는데 요: So Jesus says many things that an ordinary person could never say, and John took good care to collect those.
나는...이다. 일반 사람들은 쓰지 않는 말\n 1) 나는 생명의 떡이다:
I am.... Words ordinary people don't use
 1) I am the bread of life!
 2) I am the light of the world!
 3) I am the door of the sheep!
 4) I am the good shepherd!
 5) I am the resurrection and the life!
 6) I am the way, the truth, and the life!
 7) I am the true vine!
 - Words nobody could just say....
 - John sensed that Jesus' words were filled with self-revealing, self-proclaiming statements.
<요21:25> 예수의 행하신 일이 이 외에도 많으니 만일 낱낱이 기록된:
<John 21:25> And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which, if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written.
 - About the miracle stories, he says that if you wrote them all, even the books of this world wouldn't be enough, and he doesn't pay much attention to them, yet he records 7 very distinctive ones.
 1) Turning water into wine (beyond quality)
 - A record not found in the other Gospels
 2) The miracle of the five loaves and two fish (beyond quantity)
 - It's in the other Gospels too, but it's recorded because it's an important event beyond quantity
 3) Healing the royal official's son (beyond space)
 - He heals without even going there.
 4) Healing the sick man at Bethesda (beyond time)
 - Jesus heals even a man who had been sick for 38 years.
 5) Walking on water (beyond the laws of nature)
 - By the law of nature (the law of buoyancy), a body heavier than water should sink, but he walked.
 6) Healing the man born blind (beyond fate)
<요9:2> 제자들이 물어 가로되 랍비여 이 사람이 소경으로 난 것이 뉘:
<John 9:2> And his disciples asked him, saying, Master, who did sin, this man, or his parents, that he was born blind?
 - People back then looked at the blind and thought they were that way because of sin, but Jesus said, 'It's not because of anyone's sin. It's for the glory of God,' and healed him.
 7) Raising Lazarus from the dead (beyond death)
 - Lazarus, come forth... if he had said, “Dead, arise!” there would have been big trouble.
 - In the end, it's quietly asking the readers: if this is someone who transcends the quality of things, quantity, space, time, the laws of nature, the fate you're born with, even death, then who should we believe this person to be?
그리고 결론을 도마의 신앙고백, ‘나의 주 나의 하나님이십니다’라는데 까: And it leads the story all the way to the conclusion, Thomas's confession of faith, ‘My Lord and my God.’
6. 요한복음에만 나오는 기사\n - 요한은 사도들이 다 순교한 뒤에도:
6. Accounts found only in John
 - John remained to the very end, even after all the apostles had been martyred, looked over the other Gospels, and gathered up and put in what was missing.
 1) The wedding feast at Cana in Galilee
 2) Nicodemus coming to Jesus
 - Deep conversations show up, like the talk about being born again and the talk about God's love.
 3) Healing the sick man by the pool of Bethesda
 4) I am the good shepherd
 5) Raising Lazarus from the dead
 - It's a huge event, but it isn't in the other Gospels. Probably because Lazarus was still alive at the time.
 6) The parable of the vine
 - Matthew is someone who really collects the parables, but he left this one out.
 7) The prayer as high priest
 - Even after 60 years, he remembers all of it.
 8) Thomas's confession of faith
 - Thomas wasn't a doubter. He was someone who doubted once. He had a very thorough character, and among Jesus' disciples he had the kind of faith that never believes carelessly.
 - According to tradition, Thomas was a man who worked as a carpenter together with Jesus.
“도마야 이리 와서 네 손을 여기 넣어봐라. 그리고 믿음 없는 자가 되지: “Thomas, come here and put your hand here. And be not faithless, but believing,” Jesus said, and Thomas right away
“나의 주 나의 하나님이십니다”라고 고백했다.\n - 어설픈 신앙고백보다:
confessed, “My Lord and my God.”
 - Honest doubt is truer than a half-baked confession of faith. The first person to recognize Jesus as God was Thomas.
 9) Peter's confession of love
 - Jesus asked three times. He knew Peter's heart. Peter loved Jesus more than anyone, but because of one mistake he had even denied his sincere love; Jesus' love lets Peter say what he most wanted to say.
이 감동적인 장면에서도 물고기가 몇 마리인지 다 세어보는 요한. 두 배가:
Even in this moving scene, John counts exactly how many fish there were. Not ‘enough to sink both boats, a huge amount, enough to tear the net,’ but 153.
 10) The Christ who came from above
<요8:23> 예수께서 가라사대 너희는 아래서 났고 나는 위에서 났으며: <John 8:23> And he said unto them, Ye are from beneath; I am from above: ye are of this world; I am not of this world.
- 예수님은 위에서부터 오셨다는 이야기를 스무 번 넘게 하고 있다.\n:
- He says more than twenty times that Jesus came from above.
 11) The woman at the well in Samaria
 12) He that is without sin, let him first cast a stone
 13) The words about the Comforter, the Holy Spirit
 - In the other Gospels it's faint, only briefly mentioned in Luke, but John treats it as very important.
 14) The words giving the new commandment
 - After three years of teaching, he gives the decisive lesson: love one another. But the other disciples didn't hear it at all. They probably missed it because they were busy fighting over who was greatest, who would sit on the left and the right.
 15) A grain of wheat
 - Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit.
 16) Washing the disciples' feet
 17) Nathanael's calling
'나사렛에서 무슨 선한 것이 나겠느냐?' 막상 예수님 만나니까 '당신은:
'Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?' But when he actually meets Jesus, 'You are the Son of God; you are the King of Israel'
 18) Judas Iscariot stealing money
예수님의 머리와 발에 향유를 부은 마리아. 그 때 “그걸 팔아서 가난한:
Mary poured perfume on Jesus' head and feet. Then Judas criticized her, “You should have sold that and helped the poor, woman~” and seeing this, John writes: This he said, not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag, and bare what was put therein.
 19) He always recorded the time. It was about the sixth hour, the ninth hour, and so on.
 20) Jesus' grave clothes and the cloth folded up
 - When Peter and John heard the news that he had risen, they shot right out, ran there, and looked inside the tomb so carefully that he records that Jesus' grave clothes were lying folded, and the cloth that had wrapped his head was folded and lying by itself.
결론 - 이런 식으로 기록을 했어도 예수님의 행적을 다 기록한 것이 아니: Conclusion - even though he recorded it this way, he didn't record everything Jesus did - John 21:25
“예수께서 행하신 일이 이 외에도 많으니 만일 낱낱이 기록된다면 이 세상: “And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which, if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written.”
복음서가 4권 정도로 기록된 것, 그리고 이 정도의 이야기가 기록이 된: That the Gospels were written as about 4 books, and that this much of the story was recorded, means God saw that with just this much we can fully know who Jesus is and what kind of person he is. So we too need to study all 4 Gospels well and evenly.
